name: Nika Revolt, Justinian Nearly Overthrown
summary: The Nika Revolt erupts in Constantinople's Hippodrome when chariot-racing factional violence expands into political revolt against Justinian I's tax officials and corrupt advisers. For five days the city burns; at one point Justinian prepares to flee, but his wife Empress Theodora delivers a famous speech urging resistance ('the purple is the noblest shroud'). General Belisarius traps and massacres approximately 30,000 rebels in the Hippodrome.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Nika Revolt reveals the extreme political instability underlying Byzantine imperial authority; the Hippodrome's circus factions (Blues, Greens) are simultaneously sports clubs, political parties, and street gangs; Theodora's intervention demonstrates the decisive political role of imperial consorts in Byzantine history; the revolt's suppression enables Justinian's subsequent legislative, military, and architectural program (Hagia Sophia is rebuilt on the site of the burned church)
